newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT posts strong H1 revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT posts strong H1 revenue growth.

text.p: Czech fixed-line monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. posted flat first-half net profit on Wednesday, but strong revenue growth for the quickly developing former communist monolith had analysts singing its praises.

Interim after-tax profit dipped to 2.79 billion crowns ($81.1 million) from 2.82 billion, but total revenues rose 25 percent to 18.9 billion on strong growth in added lines and SPT's mobile phone venture.

"The consolidation of 51 percent of (mobile phone unit) EuroTel's revenues created an additional one billion crowns of revenues for SPT (first-half, year-on-year)... Eurotel now accounts for nine pecent of conolidated revenue," the company said in a statement, highlighting the results.
SPT was fixed on the Prague Stock Exchange after the earnings news at 3,826, up 26 from Tuesday's close, and then rose during real-time trading to close at 3,880, a 2.1 percent gain for the session.
The volume of trade in the stock was heavy especially in direct block trades registered on the PSE, with 153,075 shares of SPT trading at prices ranging of 3,583 to 3,840.
SPT said it had installed 218,000 net new hard lines in the six-month period, putting total lines at over three million, or 29 percent penetration of the population.

A consortium of the Dutch and Swiss PTTs won a tender for a 27 percent stake in SPT in 1995, promising to increase total line capacity to over four million by the end of the century, more than doubling its communist-era client base.

"On average, in terms of revenue, I am pretty pleased by (the results). It's in line with my expectation and in line with what can be expected from SPT," said Eugene Klerk, equities analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.

"Their number of (new) lines in the second quarter which is roughly 109,000 was below my estimate of 125,000, so obviously the revenue per line was higher than I expected, driven partly by the mobile (telephone) business," he said.
The company said 21 percent growth in total operating costs to 9.94 billion crowns slowed below revenue growth, allowing operating margins to grow 30 percent to nine billion crowns.

"Net profit is flat or almost flat which is not a disappointment because the company is in a growing phase of its development... I think that the important issue is the revenue side of the business," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.
Analysts said net profit was influenced by tax on higher depreciation claimed and should balance by year-end.
"The end-year effective tax rate should be lower because of the amount of depreciation that we're seeing as a result of the higher capital expenditure," said Trey Whalley of Atlantik FT.
SPT said that since it had larger average foreign currency balances than foreign loans, the recent sharp decline of the Czech crown was a net positive on the interim results.
"Concerning ongoing operations there is virtually no impact from the (crown's) devaluation to SPT's results," SPT said.
"SPT's exposure to the higher -- short-term -- interest rates is very limited, as most of its loans are concluded at fixed rates or tied to LIBOR," it added.

Shareholders, in June, approved a 10-for-1 stock split, to increase liquidity in the largest issue on the Prague Stock Exchange. Investor relations director Bart Morselt told Reuters that the split should be concluded by the year's end after regulatory hurdles are cleared.

"In the short-term I expect a slight drop in the share price, investors might take profits, because the price has risen sharply in the recent period. Toward the end of the year, the share price might break 4,000," said Daniel Gladis of Atlantik.
SPT said 65,000 lines were affected by recent floods in the east of the country and said some exchanges, cables and lines would have to be replaced but were covered by insurance.
The floods began in early July after the closing of the first half books.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003 ($ = 34.4 Czech Crowns)
